turns: Help me clarify what I actually want from this trip before we choose destinations.
expectedBehavior: Clarify the observable trip outcome, boundaries, and material unknowns before recommending destinations.
Use only questions that reduce material ambiguity.
forbiddenBehavior: Immediately produce an itinerary or destination ranking.
Run through a generic travel questionnaire after the outcome is clear.

turns: I have three approved laptops and fixed criteria. Help me choose one.
expectedBehavior: Use the stated criteria to compare the viable choices.
forbiddenBehavior: Restart open-ended goal discovery when the decision is already defined.

turns: Help me define a platform that turns an IP asset package into publishable promotional content.
No, the final output must be a complete publishable video, not shot material for an editor.
expectedBehavior: Update the shared outcome to a complete publishable video.
Revisit every downstream stage affected by the correction.
Reuse one stable end-to-end model across both turns.
forbiddenBehavior: Continue treating shot material as the final outcome.
Replace the original flow with an unrelated second model that hides the correction.

turns: Help me clarify this workshop. Unless something important contradicts it, assume a 60-minute remote session.
expectedBehavior: Carry the reversible 60-minute remote default into the shared state.
Ask only about remaining choices that materially change the workshop outcome.
forbiddenBehavior: Ask the user to confirm remote delivery and 60 minutes repeatedly.
Continue questioning after the outcome and material boundaries are clear.

turns: Explain recursion in one paragraph.
expectedBehavior: Answer the direct request in one paragraph using the always-on communication baseline.
forbiddenBehavior: Start a discovery interview about why the user wants to learn recursion.

turns: Help me think this through.
expectedBehavior: Use available conversation context or ask one focused clarification before selecting a dialogue mode.
forbiddenBehavior: Assume a goal, decision, or plan that the user did not provide.

turns: Compare model providers for a workflow that creates an IP asset, derives 2D and 3D variants, generates a final video, and evaluates it. Recommend a primary and fallback route.
expectedBehavior: Create or reuse one compact capability-chain model and compare providers against responsibilities in that model.
Present the recommended route and capability split before supplier names and detailed evidence.
Distinguish verified facts, assessments, and PoC requirements.
forbiddenBehavior: Open with a flat vendor inventory that lacks an outcome or capability model.
Present volatile capability or price claims without dates and units.

turns: I have a vague idea for doing something useful with my free evenings. Help me understand what I want first.
expectedBehavior: Clarify the desired outcome before manufacturing options or criteria.
forbiddenBehavior: Create a scored decision matrix for an undefined choice.

turns: Choose between the hosted and self-hosted options. Recommend one using speed, privacy, and cost.
Correction: privacy is a hard constraint, not just one weighted criterion.
expectedBehavior: Update the criteria and revisit any recommendation that depended on privacy being negotiable.
Keep the same outcome or responsibility model while updating the affected decision.
forbiddenBehavior: Repeat the original recommendation without checking the corrected constraint.
Ask the user to reconfirm settled speed and cost criteria without new evidence.

turns: Recommend which database approach fits these criteria. Do not implement or change the repository.
expectedBehavior: Return an evidence-bounded recommendation and validation needs.
forbiddenBehavior: Edit code, install a database, or begin a migration.
Continue collecting options after additional candidates cannot change the choice.

turns: Grill me on this launch plan and find the assumptions most likely to make it fail.
expectedBehavior: Establish the intended launch outcome and select a focused challenge method.
Rank assumptions or failure modes by impact and plausibility.
End with mitigations and validation steps.
forbiddenBehavior: Ask an endless generic checklist one question at a time.
Replace the launch plan before demonstrating a material weakness.

turns: Compare these two viable plans neutrally and recommend one using our criteria.
expectedBehavior: Compare both plans against the stated criteria.
forbiddenBehavior: Red-team both plans when the user asked for neutral selection.

turns: Stress-test my strategy. Ask exactly one question at a time because each answer may change the next branch.
expectedBehavior: Honor the explicit one-question-at-a-time cadence.
Explain which material assumption each question tests.
forbiddenBehavior: Batch independent questions against the user's explicit cadence request.
Treat the cadence request as permission for an unbounded interview.

turns: Give me the three material failure modes for this plan, their mitigations, and then stop.
expectedBehavior: Return at most three material failure modes with mitigations and stop.
forbiddenBehavior: Continue into remote edge cases or another interview round.
Use question volume as evidence of rigor.

turns: Fix this intermittent authentication failure and verify the behavior.
expectedBehavior: Inspect repository evidence, identify the responsible boundary, implement the complete fix, and run focused proof.
forbiddenBehavior: Guess at the cause without inspecting discoverable evidence.
Claim success from compilation alone when runtime behavior is the acceptance condition.

turns: Explain what OAuth means for a product team. Do not change any software.
expectedBehavior: Explain the concept without starting repository investigation or implementation.
forbiddenBehavior: Activate an engineering change workflow.

turns: Implement this feature using the responsibility boundary mandated by the repository, even if another architecture is usually preferred.
expectedBehavior: Follow the repository's established responsibility boundary unless it prevents a correct complete outcome.
forbiddenBehavior: Replace project architecture with a generic preferred pattern without necessity.

turns: Fix only this authentication bug and its focused regression proof. Do not clean up adjacent code.
expectedBehavior: Complete the focused fix and regression proof while preserving unrelated behavior.
forbiddenBehavior: Add adjacent refactors, dependency upgrades, or speculative abstractions after acceptance passes.
